name: Ahab
bio: Ahab son of Omri succeeded his father as king of Israel, reigning twenty-two years in Samaria (1 Kings 16:28-29). Scripture introduces him with a damning verdict: he did more evil in the LORD's eyes than any king of Israel before him. As if walking in the sins of Jeroboam were a trivial thing, he married Jezebel, daughter of Ethbaal, king of the Sidonians, and went on to serve and worship Baal, building a temple and altar for Baal in Samaria and making an Asherah pole — provoking the LORD to anger more than any king of Israel before him (1 Kings 16:30-33). In his reign, Hiel of Bethel rebuilt Jericho, losing his firstborn son Abiram when he laid its foundations and his youngest son Segub when he set up its gates, in grim fulfillment of the curse Joshua had pronounced centuries earlier on anyone who rebuilt that city (1 Kings 16:34; compare Joshua 6:26). It was against this backdrop that the prophet Elijah confronted Ahab directly, announcing a drought that would last for years except at his word — a direct challenge to Baal, the storm god Ahab now served (1 Kings 17:1). Ahab's long, consequential reign — his marriage to Jezebel, his conflicts with the prophet Elijah, his wars, and his death — is told in detail in the chapters ahead.
